outputs.exact_statement: Let $M$ be a connected noncompact complex manifold of complex dimension $n\geq1$. If $M$ admits a smooth complete Kähler metric with strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature, then $M$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb C^n$.

The following objects and estimates are available.* 1. *There is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic function $\psi$ with $\psi\le C(1+r)$.* 2. *Holomorphic functions and holomorphic tangent fields interpolate arbitrary finite jets at a finite set of points. There are finitely many holomorphic functions defining an injective immersion $F:M\mathrel{% \BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,space=false,pdfliteral=direct,ActualText=27F6}% \longrightarrow% \EndAccSupp{pdfliteral=direct}% }\mathbb C^N$, and finitely many global holomorphic tangent fields spanning $T^{1,0}M$ at every point.* 3. *At every point $x$ there is a global holomorphic canonical section $S$ with $S(x)\ne0$ and $\log|S|_g^2\le C_S(1+r)$. There is also a smooth function $\Xi$ such that $$\label{prelim:xi} \partial\bar\partial\Xi\ge\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}(g),\qquad \Xi\le C(1+r^{3/2}).$$* 4. *There is a smooth exhaustion $u\ge1$ such that $$\label{prelim:exhaustion} C^{-1}(1+r)\le u\le C(1+r),\qquad |\partial u|_g\le C,\qquad |\partial\bar\partial u|_g\le C/u.$$* 5. *If $S(o)\ne0$ is chosen as in (iii), then, for $L\ge1$, $$\label{prelim:averages} \frac{1}{\mathop{\mathrm{Vol}}B(o,L)}\int_{B(o,L)} \bigl|\log|S|_g^2\bigr|\,dV_g\le CL, \qquad \frac{1}{\mathop{\mathrm{Vol}}B(o,L)}\int_{B(o,L)}R_g\,dV_g\le C/L.$$* *Neither $F$ nor $\psi$ is asserted to be proper. The exhaustion in (iv) has a two-sided complex Hessian bound.

For every sufficiently large fixed integer $k$, there is a positive function $\chi(x,t)$ on $M\times[0,T]$, smooth in space and continuously differentiable in time one-sided at the initial surface, such that $$\label{flow:cutoff-bounds}
 \begin{gathered}
 C_T^{-1}u^{-k}\le\chi\le C_Tu^{-k},\qquad
 |\partial\chi|_g\le C_T\chi/u,\\
 \partial\bar\partial\chi\le C_T\chi h_t,
 \qquad \partial_t\chi\le C_T(1+t^{\beta-1})\chi
 \quad(t>0).
 \end{gathered}$$

Fix a finite $T>0$. The following conclusions hold for the flow of Theorem 4.* 1. *The function $\rho$ is the minimal nonnegative solution with zero initial values of $$\label{flow:rho-source} (\partial_t-\Delta_{h_t})\rho =\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{h_t}\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}(g).$$ There are nonnegative smooth supercaloric functions $\rho_j$ on $M\times[0,T]$ such that $$\label{flow:rho-tails} 0\le\rho_j\le\rho,\qquad \rho_j\ge\rho-C_j,\qquad \rho_j\mathrel{% \BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,space=false,pdfliteral=direct,ActualText=27F6}% \longrightarrow% \EndAccSupp{pdfliteral=direct}% }0 \text{ locally uniformly on }M\times[0,T].$$ Each fixed $\rho_j$ has all spatial and one-sided time derivatives smooth at $t=0$ and bounded on compact spacetime sets.* 2. *Suppose $v$ is upper semicontinuous, bounded on compact spacetime sets, $0\le v\le\rho$, and satisfies, in the upper viscosity sense on $0

Fix $T>0$ and let $v$ be upper semicontinuous, bounded on compact spacetime sets, and satisfy $0\le v\le\rho$ on $M\times[0,T]$. Suppose that $v$ satisfies [flow:nonlinear-comparison] in the upper viscosity sense for $0

For each compact $K\subset M$ and each $A_0<\infty$, there is a compact $K'\subset M$ such that every holomorphic disc $f:\overline\Delta\to M$, smooth up to the circle, satisfying $$f(\partial\Delta)\subset K,\qquad
 \int_\Delta f^*\omega_g\le A_0$$ has $f(\overline\Delta)\subset K'$. Every sequence of such discs has a subsequence converging holomorphically on compact subsets of $\Delta$.*

*The same statements hold for discs in $Y$ with compact boundary in $Y$ and with $\int_\Delta(\pi\circ f)^*\omega_g\le A_0$. The resulting compact may depend on $K$ and $A_0$.

Let $(E,k)$ be a smooth Hermitian holomorphic vector bundle on $\Delta^*=\{0<|z|<1\}$, with Griffiths nonnegative curvature. Suppose that $A:E\to\Delta^*\times\mathbb C^q$ is holomorphic, pointwise injective, and has bounded operator norm. If $a$ is a holomorphic section with $\int_{\Delta^*}|a|_k^2\,dA<\infty$, then there are $r_0>0$ and $\sigma>0$ such that $$\label{disc:extra-integrability}
 \int_{0<|z|<r_0}|a|_k^2|z|^{-\sigma}\,dA<\infty.$$ The exponent may depend on the section and the bundle data.

Let $\Omega_j$ be increasing open subsets exhausting a connected complex manifold $X$, and let $u_j$ be plurisubharmonic on $\Omega_j$. Assume that for each compact $K\subset X$, the functions $u_j$ are uniformly bounded above on $K$ once $K\subset\Omega_j$. Every sequence has a subsequence for which either $u_j$ tends to $-\infty$ locally uniformly from above, or $u_j$ converges in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ to a plurisubharmonic function. A lower bound $u_j(z_j)\ge-A$ at points $z_j$ in a fixed compact set excludes the first alternative along that sequence. In particular, lower bounds on moving subsets of a fixed compact set of uniformly positive measure suffice. If the $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ limit is the constant $c$, then $$\limsup_j\sup_K u_j\le c$$ for every compact $K\subset X$.

Let $L$ be an $r\times r$ smooth Hermitian matrix on the circle with $mI\le L\le MI$, where $0<m\le M<\infty$. There is a holomorphic invertible matrix $H$ on $\Delta$, smooth with smooth inverse on $\overline\Delta$, such that $L=H^*H$ on the circle. It satisfies $$\begin{aligned}
 \|H\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}&\le\sqrt M,&
 \|H^{-1}\|_{\infty,\mathrm{op}}&\le m^{-1/2},\label{disc:factor-sup}\\
 D(H)^2&\le\frac{M}{2m^2}D(L)^2,&
 D(H^{-1})^2&\le\frac1{2m^3}D(L)^2.
 \label{disc:factor-seminorm}
\end{aligned}$$ In particular the seminorm constants depend only on the boundary spectral bounds, independently of higher derivatives of $L$.

Suppose that a smooth real function $\varphi$ touches $v$ from below at $(y_*,s_*)$, where $0<s_*<T$. In holomorphic cotangent coordinates write $$W=\partial\bar\partial_Y\varphi(y_*,s_*)=
 \begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ B^*&C\end{pmatrix},\qquad C>0.$$ There is a Hermitian form $K$ on the horizontal coordinate space such that $$K\ge0,\qquad K\ge A-BC^{-1}B^*,\qquad
 \partial_s\varphi(y_*,s_*)\ge\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(C^{\mathsf T}K).
 \label{var:viscosity-inequality}$$ The transpose is the tangent–cotangent contraction in these coordinates. In particular the statement applies to lower tests translated in a fixed cotangent coordinate chart; its contraction has constant coefficients.

Use the preceding localization, with $j$ sufficiently large and $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small that the minimizing-sequence centers have a common interior margin in $\mathcal C$. Fix a bound $L<\infty$ and such a sequence for [var:penalized-functional], with energy bounded by $E_0<\infty$. Let $l_\nu$ be any holomorphic columns, smooth on the closed disc, such that $$\|l_\nu\|_\infty\le L,\qquad D(l_\nu)\le D_0<\infty.$$ They may depend on the disc. With $\varphi_{E,c}=E_f(0)^*\partial\bar\partial_Y\varphi(f(0),s)E_f(0)$, one has $$\limsup_{\nu\to\infty} \left\{ h(0)^2\varphi_{E,c}(l(0),\overline{l(0)}) -\langle T_b(l,\bar l)\rangle -C_j(L)\varepsilon\bigl(1+\mathcal E+D(l)^2\bigr) \right\}\le0. \label{var:deformation-estimate}$$ The constant $C_j(L)$ depends only on $L$, the dimension, the chosen integer $a$, the fixed time interval and center cylinder, and smooth coefficient bounds for the metrics, immersion, Gauss map and cutoffs on a fixed neighborhood of the boundary compact $K_j$. It is independent of $\varepsilon,E_0,D_0$, of the interior compact $K_{j,\varepsilon}'$, and of the auxiliary loss introduced in the proof. In contrast, the existence radius of the deformations, bounds on their full coefficients, and bounds on Taylor remainders may depend on $j,L,E_0,D_0,K_{j,\varepsilon}'$, that loss, the interior margin of the centers, and the fixed smooth test $\varphi$.

In a cotangent vector space with canonical bivector $\mathcal J=\sum_i e_i\wedge f_i$, let $\mathcal H>0$ be Hermitian, and suppose $\mathcal H\ge W$, where the vertical block $C$ of $W$ is positive. Then $$S=\mathop{\mathrm{Schur}}(\mathcal H)\ge0,\qquad
 S\ge\mathop{\mathrm{Schur}}(W),\qquad p(\mathcal H)\ge\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(C^{\mathsf T}S).
 \label{var:schur-cost}$$

For the flow in Theorem 4, the function $$(x,\xi,w)\mathrel{% \BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,space=false,pdfliteral=direct,ActualText=27FC}% {\let\mathrel{% \BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,space=false,pdfliteral=direct,ActualText=27F6}% \longrightarrow% \EndAccSupp{pdfliteral=direct}% }\longrightarrow\longmapsto}% \EndAccSupp{pdfliteral=direct}% }N(x,\xi,e^{w+\bar w})$$ is plurisubharmonic on $T^{*(1,0)}M\times\mathbb C$. For every finite $T$, its disc envelope satisfies $v=N$ on $T^{*(1,0)}M\times(0,T)$.

For every fixed compact $K\subset M$, there are $r_K,c_K,C_K>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $t$ and every $p\in K$, there is a holomorphic local biholomorphism $$\Phi:B_{\mathbb C^n}(r_K)\mathrel{%
  \BeginAccSupp{method=hex,unicode,space=false,pdfliteral=direct,ActualText=27F6}%
  \longrightarrow%
  \EndAccSupp{pdfliteral=direct}%
}M,\qquad
 \Phi(0)=p,\qquad d\Phi(0)\text{ unitary for }h_t,$$ with $c_Kg_{\rm eucl}\le\Phi^*h_t\le C_Kg_{\rm eucl}$. The pullback metrics have bounds of every fixed derivative order on smaller balls. The corresponding local smooth compactness statement holds for rescaled flows whenever curvature is uniformly bounded on fixed-radius moving balls during a fixed two-sided time interval.

Fix $r,c>0$ and a compact set $K\subset M$. Suppose $\Phi:B_{\mathbb C^n}(r)\to M$ is a holomorphic local biholomorphism, $\Phi(0)\in K$, and $\widetilde g=\Phi^*g\ge c g_{\rm eucl}$. Let $A$ and $B$ be the least and greatest singular lengths of $d\Phi(0)$, using the Euclidean metric in the domain and $g$ in the target. There are constants depending only on $K,r,c$ and the initial geometry on a compact neighborhood of $K$ such that $$\label{chart:static-distortion}
 B\le C(1+A)^C.$$ In particular these constants are independent of the particular chart and its total distortion.
The manifold $M$ is simply connected.
Every bounded-above plurisubharmonic function on $M$ is constant, including a function which is not assumed continuous.

For fixed $n,d$, every invertible constant-volume $d$-jet fixing zero is the $d$-jet of a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb C^n$. Its degree and inverse degree are bounded by a constant $D_d$. Its coefficients and inverse coefficients are bounded polynomially in the coefficients of the given jet and its inverse linear part. These bounds do not depend on the grid or on $h$.

On every run of regular steps there are unipotent matrices $L_k^+$, with off-diagonal entries only in rows of smaller weight than their columns, such that, on putting $L_k^-=D_k^{-1}L_k^+D_k$, the diagonal step derivative remains $D_k$ and every regular jump becomes $$J_k=L_{k+1}^-U_k(L_k^+)^{-1},\qquad
 (J_k)_{il}=0\quad\hbox{if }w_{k+1,i}<w_{k,l}.
 \label{eq:dyn:aligned-jump}$$ The matrices $L_k^+$ and their inverses have polynomial bounds in the macro index $j$, while $$\lVert L_k^- -I\rVert
 \le j^C\exp\left(-c\frac{\sqrt{S_j}}{j^2}\right).
 \label{eq:dyn:small-start-change}$$ The estimates are uniform in finite terminal horizons, and hold on an infinite regular run by a coefficientwise limit.

The flag threshold $M$ can be chosen so that regular macro starts occur arbitrarily late, and the polynomial models constructed above, initialized at any sufficiently late such start, satisfy [eq:dyn:forward-degree].

For either raw sequence above and every sufficiently large $k$, $$\xi_k=\lim_{l\to\infty}G_{k,l}^{-1}\zeta_l$$ exists locally uniformly in the indicated variables. It is holomorphic and satisfies $$\lvert\xi_k-\zeta_k\rvert\le e^{-6s_k},\qquad \xi_{k+1}=G_k\xi_k. \label{eq:unif:shadow}$$ All applications of [eq:unif:inverse-tube] take place inside its stated balls.

The locally uniform limit on the exhaustion $$\Psi(x)=\lim_{l\to\infty}G_{0,l}^{-1}H_lf_{s_l}(x)
 \label{eq:unif:global-map}$$ defines an injective holomorphic map $M\to\mathbb C^n$ with $\Psi(o)=0$. Its image $\Omega$ is open, and $\Psi:M\to\Omega$ is a biholomorphism. Moreover, on every compact $K\subset\Omega$, $$\sup_K\lvert G_{0,k}\rvert\le e^{-(\sigma/2)s_k}
 \quad\hbox{eventually},
 \label{eq:unif:forward-smallness}$$ and, at every sufficiently large $k$, $$G_{0,k}^{-1}\bigl(B(e^{-\gamma's_k})\bigr)\subset\Omega.
 \label{eq:unif:inverse-ball-inclusion}$$
